'''Terence B. Davis II''' (born May 16, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss Rebels]]. After going [[List of undrafted NBA players|undrafted]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]], he signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in 2020. He has also played for the [[Sacramento Kings]].

==Early life==
Davis is the son of Trinina Smith and Terence Davis Sr. He began playing basketball at the age of six. He became a star football player at [[Southaven High School]], competing as a [[wide receiver]]. Davis also managed to make the state's freestyle swimming finals in 2015. Davis earned twenty scholarship offers from major universities for football but opted to pursue basketball in college instead.<ref name="dortch">{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Dortch|title=Ole Miss' Terence Davis ready for any NBA role|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/06/06/ole-miss-terence-davis-ready-nba-role|website=NBA.com|date=June 6, 2019|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
Davis played sparingly as a freshman at Ole Miss, averaging 1.9 points and 6.9 minutes per game. Coach [[Andy Kennedy]]'s advice was to become a ball-getter and he improved markedly as a sophomore, becoming one of the most improved players in all of college basketball, and scoring 30 points on 6-for-7 three-pointers in an NIT win over [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]].<ref name="dortch"/> He averaged 14.9 points and 5.3 rebounds per game as a sophomore. In his junior season, Davis led the team in scoring with 13.8 points per game, while contributing 6.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Bryan|last=Flynn|title=Terence Davis: Improving NBA Draft Stock|url=http://www.jacksonfreepress.com/news/2019/jun/14/terence-davis-improving-nba-draft-stock/|work=[[Jackson Free Press]]|date=June 14, 2019|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref>

After the season, coach Kennedy was fired and [[Kermit Davis]], who was named SEC coach of the year in 2019, was tapped as the new coach. As a senior, Davis posted 15.2 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game while shooting his best three-point percentage and free throw percentage of his career at 37.1% and 77.2%, respectively.<ref name="dortch"/> He was named SEC player of the week after scoring 27 points and pulling down 12 rebounds, in a win over [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] on January 9, 2019. Davis was named to the All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] second team.<ref>{{cite web|title=SEC Pegs Davis as Coach of the Year, T.D. and Tyree All-SEC|url=https://247sports.com/college/ole-miss/Article/SEC-Pegs-Davis-as-Coach-of-the-Year-TD-and-Tyree-All-SEC-129986421/|website=247Sports.com|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref> During his career at Ole Miss, Davis led the team to the NCAA tournament for the ninth time in school history. After the season Davis participated in the Portsmouth Invitational Tournament and was named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref name="dortch"/>

==Professional career==
===Toronto Raptors (2019–2021)===
After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Davis joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the NBA Summer League.<ref>{{cite news|first=Nathanael|last=Gabler|title=Terence Davis signs UDFA contract with Denver Nuggets|url=https://www.oxfordeagle.com/2019/06/22/terence-davis-signs-udfa-contract-with-denver-nuggets/|work=[[The Oxford Eagle]]|date=June 22, 2019|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref> On July 11, 2019, Davis signed a two-year deal with the [[Toronto Raptors]], with a full guarantee in year one.<ref>{{cite news|title=Raptors Sign Terence Davis|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-terence-davis|website=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2019|access-date=July 11, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|title=Feels good to wake up a Raptor🙏🏾💯 What’s up The North👀|number=1148261506301091840|user=TerenceDavisJr|date=July 8, 2019|access-date=October 5, 2024}}</ref> On October 22, 2019, Davis made his debut in NBA, coming off the bench in a 130–122 overtime win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] with five points, five rebounds, two assists and two steals.<ref>{{cite web|title=VanVleet scores career-high 34, Raptors top Pelicans 130-122|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160623|website=ESPN.com|date=October 22, 2019|access-date=October 22, 2019}}</ref> On November 20, Davis put up impressive numbers in 113–97 win over the Orlando Magic, scoring 19 points and grabbing 8 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Terence Davis Game by Game Stats and Performance|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3919454/terence-davis|website=ESPN.com|access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref> On January 8, in his first career start, Davis scored 23 points to go along with 11 rebounds and 5 assists, leading the Raptors to a 112–110 overtime win against the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Reed|title=Terence Davis goes from zero to hero as exhausted Raptors scrape by Hornets in OT|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/toronto-raptors-charlotte-hornets-recap-sports-1.5420145|work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 8, 2020|access-date=January 9, 2020}}</ref> On February 2, 2020, Davis scored a career-high 31 points against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. During the [[Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season|NBA hiatus]], he worked out in Miami. Including the seeding games in the [[2020 NBA Bubble]], Davis was the only Raptor to play all 72 regular-season games for the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]]. On September 15, 2020, Davis was named [[NBA All-Rookie Team|2019–20 NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] by the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ja Morant, Zion Williamsom headline 2019-20 Kia All-Rookie First Team Tyler Herro, Rui Hachimura voted to Second Team|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/15/nba-2019-20-all-rookie-first-team-official-release|website=NBA.com|date=September 15, 2020|access-date=September 15, 2020}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2021–2023)===
On March 25, 2021, Davis was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for a 2021 second-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Acquire Terence Davis|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-terence-davis|website=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021|access-date=February 5, 2023}}</ref> He made his Kings debut two days later, recording six points, two rebounds and two assists in a 100–98 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=KINGS BEAT CAVS ON BARNES' 3-POINTER AT THE BUZZER|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000702|website=NBA.com|date=March 27, 2021|access-date=February 5, 2023}}</ref>

On August 7, 2021, Davis re-signed with the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Re-Sign Terence Davis|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-re-sign-terence-davis|website=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021|access-date=February 5, 2023}}</ref> He scored a career-high 35 points in a 133–131 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]] on January 19, 2022.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pistons pull off stunning rally to beat Kings|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-nba-sac-det/pistons-pull-off-stunning-rally-to-beat-kings-idUSMTZXEI1KZVCW32|website=Reuters.com|date=January 19, 2022|access-date=January 20, 2022}}</ref> On February 1, 2022, Davis underwent wrist surgery and was ruled out for three months, effectively ending the rest of his regular-season run.<ref>{{cite web|title=Terence Davis Medical Update|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/terence-davis-medical-update-0|website=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2022}}</ref>

On November 15, 2022, Davis scored 31 points, grabbed nine rebounds, and recorded three steals and seven three-pointers at 70% field goal shooting, in a 153–121 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Dierberger|title=TD credits Brown after making NBA history in Kings' statement win|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/terence-davis-makes-nba-history-kings-statement-win-credits-mike-brown|website=NBCSports.com|date=November 17, 2022|access-date=November 17, 2022}}</ref>

===Rip City Remix (2023–2024)===
On December 11, 2023, Davis joined the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Rip City Remix|title=Welcome to Rip City, @terencedavisjr 💿‼️|number=1734313894641123581|user=ripcityremix|date=December 11, 2023|access-date=December 13, 2023}}</ref> However, he left the Remix in January 2024, after suffering a season-ending injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Terence Davis: Suffers Achilles rupture|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/terence-davis-suffers-achilles-rupture/|website=CBSSports.com|date=January 17, 2024|access-date=January 23, 2024}}</ref>

===Wisconsin Herd (2024–2025)===
On October 2, 2024, Davis signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Terence Davis Signs Exhibit 10 Contract With Bucks|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/terence-davis-to-sign-exhibit-10-contract-with-bucks.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 3, 2024|access-date=October 5, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 15.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Bucks’ Terence Davis, Cavs’ Zhaire Smith Waived|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/bucks-waive-terence-davis.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> On October 28, he joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref>{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCES 2024-25 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announces-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}}</ref>

===Second stint with Kings (2025)===
On April 9, 2025, Davis returned to the Sacramento Kings.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 9, 2025 |title=Kings Sign Terence Davis |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-terence-davis |access-date=May 18, 2025 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He was waived by Sacramento prior to the start of the regular season on October 18,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings Waive Terence Davis|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-terence-davis|access-date=November 25, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> and joined the [[Stockton Kings]]. Davis was waived by the Kings on February 3, 2026.

On February 6, 2026, he was announced by the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] as their new signing for the upcoming season in [[Puerto Rico]]'s [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>https://www.instagram.com/p/DUalryTkUwT/?igsh=cjVrd2I5eDVhN2Rt</ref> He was released from the team on April 23, when the Leones signed [[Darius Bazley]].

==Personal life==
Davis was arrested in New York City on October 27, 2020, after allegedly slapping his girlfriend in the face and breaking her cell phone.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 28, 2020 |title=Raptors' Davis arrested in New York after allegedly assaulting girlfriend in which charges were later dropped |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-davis-arrested-new-york-allegedly-assaulting-girlfriend/ |access-date=November 1, 2020 |website=Sportsnet.ca |agency=Canadian Press}}</ref> The charges were reportedly dropped a few months later.<ref>{{cite web | title=Report: Charges vs. Raptors' Davis dropped | website=TSN | date=2025-07-10 | url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/report-charges-dropped-against-toronto-raptors-guard-terence-davis-1.1595554 | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>
